The second line mentions a black fate (bekt siyah) like the smoke of a lamp (sham) that has a canopy (chetrzdeh) over my head. This sounds like a person is enduring suffering (tears not falling, which might be a metaphor for holding back emotions) and their bad fortune is covering them like smoke from a lamp. So the theme here is about enduring hardship, perhaps with a sense of hope that one day they will rise (become dawn), but currently being under a dark fate.

Option 3 is about enduring a bad fate (bekt siyah) and waiting for the dawn (sahr) to come, which is similar to option 1.
